title: ZDX Score analysis jobs through the API: starting one, polling it, and what the clients return

prose.text: A score analysis is an asynchronous job: one call starts it and returns an ID, and another reads its progress and result. The endpoints and client functions are generated (`node scripts/kb.mjs surface zdx`).

prose.label: The contract.
prose.text: {{contract-start}} {{contract-result}} {{postman-start-body}} Its keys differ from the contract's {{divergence:postman-body-keys}}.

prose.label: Go and MCP.
prose.text: The Go start function returns no decoded body: [[zdx.sdk-go.service-defects:no-decode-functions]]. The MCP analysis reader is the only ZDX tool that converts timestamps: [[zdx.diagnostics.mcp-tools:timestamp-conversion]].

checks.do: Where the analysis ID came from: neither the Python start result nor the Go start function hands it back decoded.

contract-start.statement: The contract's analysis start takes `device_id`, `app_id` and `t0` (required) and `t1`, all int64 integers, for a score analysis of an app between t0 and t1, and answers with `analysis_id`, the ID used to track progress and get the result, and a `status`.

expect.description: Start Score Analysis for a given app between t0 and t1
Score analysis ID. Use this ID for tracking the progress and get the result

contract-result.statement: Reading an analysis returns `analysis_id`, `status`, `err_msg` and a `result` holding `issue`, `confidence`, `message` and `times`, the time points where the issue is seen.

expect.description: Track the analysis progress and get results

times.description: Time points where the issue is seen

python-start.statement: The Python `start_analysis` sends its keyword arguments as the body and builds its result as a `DeviceApplicationAnalysis`, which reads only `device_id`, `app_id`, `t0` and `t1`.

quotes: self.device_id = config["device_id"] if "device_id" in config else None
self.app_id = config["app_id"] if "app_id" in config else None
self.t0 = config["t0"] if "t0" in config else None
self.t1 = config["t1"] if "t1" in config else None

python-start.conditions: The four quoted assignments are every attribute the model's constructor sets at the pin.

python-start-loses-id.statement: So the object the Python `start_analysis` returns carries none of the `analysis_id` and `status` the contract's start response holds, and the ID needed to poll the job has to be read from the raw response.
python-start-loses-id.conditions: Follows from the model's attribute list against the contract's response fields; not observed against a live tenant.

python-get-raw.statement: The Python `get_analysis` returns a one-element list holding `form_response_body` applied to the response body, with no model class around it; for a JSON object body `form_response_body` builds and returns a dict.

postman-start-body.statement: The OneAPI Postman collection's Start Score Analysis request sends `deviceid` (a quoted string), `appid` (filled from `{{appID}}`), `t0` and `t1`.

postman-body-keys.summary: The analysis start body's ID keys: the contract requires `device_id` and `app_id`; the Postman example sends `deviceid` and `appid`.

positions.says: The Postman start body names the IDs `deviceid` and `appid`.

postman-body-keys.impact: A request copied from the collection lacks two keys the contract marks required; no source says whether the API accepts the unseparated names.
